insights.title: 2 mechanical single-tool calls spent over 2k thinking tokens each (4.3k total)
insights.recommendation: Thinking tokens are output tokens: the model generates them one at a time, so they add latency as well as volume, and a routine Read or status check rarely needs them. Lower the effort for mechanical steps (/effort medium, or effort in an agent’s frontmatter); keep high effort for the hard ones, where thinking is the point.

insights.title: Recorded MCP instruction and deferred-tool payloads total 52,060 bytes
insights.recommendation: Review these recorded payloads if their size matters to the task. Byte counts cover observed occurrences only; they do not establish per-request persistence, schema loading, unused servers, or token savings.

insights.title: Agent type 'general-purpose' is 91% mechanical on Claude Sonnet 5 (3.43M tokens in those requests)
insights.recommendation: A mostly-mechanical agent type (single tool call, tiny output, no thinking) does not need the frontier model: set model: haiku in that agent’s frontmatter or the Agent call. It will send the same tokens either way. What you get back is a faster turn and the big model left free for the judgment-heavy agents.

evidence.criteria: mechanical = exactly 1 tool_use, < 200 output tokens, no reported thinking; grouped per agent type × model; fires at >= 10 mechanical and >= 60% share on a non-haiku model
